ja.text: ブラジルナッツは、サガリバナ科の高木 、またはナッツとして食用にされるその種子である。

en.text: Brazil nut refers to a South American tree of the monotypic genus Bertholletia in the family Lecythidaceae as well as the tree's commercially-harvested edible seeds. It is one of the largest and longest-lived trees in the Amazon rainforest. The fruit and its nutshell – containing the edible nut – are relatively large and weigh as much as 2 kg (4.4 lb) in total. As food, Brazil nuts are notable for diverse content of micronutrients, especially a high amount of selenium. The wood of the Brazil nut tree is prized for its quality in carpentry, flooring, and heavy construction.

es.text: Bertholletia excelsa es un árbol de la familia Lecythidaceae, nativo de Sudamérica, endémico de la Amazonía, específicamente de Bolivia, Brasil, el sudeste de Colombia, Guyana, Perú y el sur de Venezuela. Sus semillas son comestibles y reciben varios nombres: avellana del Brasil, castaña del Brasil, coquito de Brasil, nuez de Pará, nuez amazónica, nuez boliviana, nuez de Brasil, castaña de Pará y castaña de monte.

fr.text: Le Noyer du Brésil, Châtaignier du Brésil ou Noyer d’Amazonie est une espèce de plantes à fleurs, de la famille des Lecythidaceae. Il est disséminé dans les forêts tropicales chaudes et humides qui longent le fleuve Amazone et son affluant le rio Negro situées au Brésil. On le retrouve aussi en Bolivie, au Pérou, en Colombie et au Venezuela. C’est l'un des plus grands arbres de la forêt amazonienne et peut mesurer plus de 50 m de haut, d'où son surnom de roi de la forêt amazonienne. Il produit la noix du Brésil formée d’une coque épaisse et dure d’une dizaine de centimètres de diamètre. Cette noix contient une vingtaine de graines protégées par un tégument lignifié. Cette graine, une amande blanche comestible, est particulièrement riche en lipide, en sélénium et zinc, ainsi qu'en fibres, phosphore, magnésium, fer et vitamine E.

pt.text: Bertholletia excelsa ou castanheira é uma árvore de grande porte da família Lecitidácea, originária da floresta de terra firme, muito abundante na Amazônia, cujo fruto contém a castanha, do qual se extrai o núcleo de sua semente para o consumo. A primeira menção registrada remonta a 1596, realizada por Juan Álvarez Maldonado, nas matas do território que hoje corresponde ao Peru.

id.text: Kacang Brasil adalah sebuah pohon Amerika Selatan dalam keluarga Lecythidaceae, dan juga nama benih pohon yang dapat dimakan secara komersial. Ini adalah salah satu pohon terbesar dan berumur panjang di hutan hujan Amazon. Buah dan kulitnya—mengandung kacang Brazil yang dapat dimakan—relatif besar, mungkin beratnya mencapai 2 kilogram. Sebagai makanan, kacang Brasil terkenal karena kandungan mikronutrien yang beragam, terutama selenium dalam jumlah tinggi. Kayu pohon kacang Brasil dihargai karena kualitasnya dalam pertukangan kayu, lantai, dan konstruksi berat.

en.heading: Toxicity
en.text:
Brazil nuts are susceptible to contamination by aflatoxins, produced by fungi, once they fall to the ground. Aflatoxins can cause liver damage, including possible cancer, if consumed. Aflatoxin levels have been found in Brazil nuts during inspections that were far higher than the limits set by the EU. However, mechanical sorting and drying was found to eliminate 98% of aflatoxins; a 2003 EU ban on importation was rescinded after new tolerance levels were set.
The nuts may contain traces of radium, a radioactive element, with a kilogram of nuts containing an activity between 40 and 260 becquerels (1 and 7 nanocuries); although a small dose of radium, this exposure is higher than in common foods. According to Oak Ridge Associated Universities, elevated levels of radium in the soil do not directly cause the concentration of radium, but "the very extensive root system of the tree" can concentrate naturally occurring radioactive material, when present in the soil. Radium can be concentrated in nuts only if it is present in the soil.
Brazil nuts also contain barium, a metal with a chemical behavior quite similar to radium. While barium can have toxic side effects when ingested (weakness, vomiting, diarrhea, etc.) the amount present in Brazil nuts is too small to have noticeable health effects.

en.heading: Uses
en.text:
■ Wood
The lumber from Brazil nut trees (not to be confused with Brazilwood) is of excellent quality, having diverse uses from flooring to heavy construction. Logging the trees is prohibited by law in all three producing countries (Brazil, Bolivia, and Peru). Illegal extraction of timber and land clearances present continuing threats. In Brazil, cutting down a Brazil nut tree requires previous authorization from the Brazilian Institute of Environment and Renewable Natural Resources.

■ Other uses
Brazil nut oil is used as a lubricant in clocks and in the manufacturing of paint and cosmetics, such as soap and perfume. 
Because of its hardness, the Brazil nutshell is often pulverized and used as an abrasive to polish materials, such as metals and ceramics, in the same way as jeweler's rouge, while charcoal from the shells can be used to purify water.

pt.heading: Uso medicinal
pt.text:
O chá da casca da Bertholletia excelsa é usado na Amazônia para tratamento do fígado, e a infusão de suas sementes para problemas estomacais.
A castanha é uma rica fonte de magnésio, tiamina e possui as mais altas concentrações conhecidas de selênio (126 ppm²), com propriedades antioxidantes. A presença desses antioxidantes combateria os radicais livres. Algumas pesquisas indicaram que o consumo de selênio está relacionado com a redução do risco de câncer de próstata e recomendaram o consumo da semente como uma medida preventiva. Porém, revisão por pares e estudos subsequentes sobre o efeito do selênio no câncer de próstata foram inconclusivos.
Extratos do óleo da castanha são usados como umidificador de pele com ressecamento.
